import requests, sys, uuid, json, time

BASE = '{{TESTVDB_DB_URL}}'

# Test idempotency on create_collection: create same collection twice with same params
# First call should succeed, second call (idempotent) should also succeed with same result
c = 'tc_idemp_' + uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]
print(f"Testing collection: {c}")

body = {
    "vectors": {
        "size": 4,
        "distance": "Cosine"
    }
}

# First call - create collection
r1 = requests.put(f'{BASE}/collections/{c}', json=body)
print(f"First create: Status={r1.status_code}, Response={r1.text[:200]}")
time.sleep(0.5)

# Second call - try to create same collection again (idempotent)
r2 = requests.put(f'{BASE}/collections/{c}', json=body)
print(f"Second create: Status={r2.status_code}, Response={r2.text[:200]}")

# For idempotency, both should succeed (409 conflict is also acceptable for duplicate)
# But if second returns error, that's not truly idempotent
if r1.status_code in (200, 201) and r2.status_code in (200, 201):
    print(f"Idempotency OK: both calls succeeded")
    sys.exit(0)
elif r1.status_code in (200, 201) and r2.status_code == 409:
    print(f"Idempotency OK: first created, second reported conflict (acceptable for idempotency)")
    sys.exit(0)
elif r1.status_code in (200, 201) and r2.status_code == 400:
    print(f"[DEFECT: STATE_VIOLATION] Second create returned 400 - not idempotent")
    sys.exit(1)
else:
    print(f"First create status: {r1.status_code}, Second create status: {r2.status_code}")
    sys.exit(0)
